ai.subscriptionTitle: Or sign in with a subscription, no key:

projectTasks.intro: The project's executors implement an approved rule through checks: QA writes tests that fail on the current code, the developer makes them pass without touching the tests, and you review the changes and accept them into the app. If the rule is already implemented and you approved a new version, the task becomes a change: QA rewrites this rule's tests, other rules' tests stay as they were. Each works in its own copy; the app itself changes only when you accept.

projectTasks.limits: Accepting the work is your decision: the reviewer's verdict is advice, but accepting over "changes requested" takes a separate tick. Finishing a stage is confirmed with a button — the panel does not guess that an agent is done. The app and the tests run in separate containers when the tests take the app's address from CLAWDESK_APP_URL (as in the template); in older projects the tests start the app themselves, in one isolation with its code, and the card warns about it. The developer may not change tests, and QA may not change other rules' tests or the existing shared test code. A test belongs to a rule if its name starts with the rule's code or it is linked to one of its scenarios. Only the latest accepted task can be rolled back, and only while the app has not changed since. A project has one task at a time.

workItems.title: Company tasks
workItems.scope: You set a task: what to do, acceptance criteria, executor, deadline. An executor has one task in work; the rest wait in its queue and start by themselves when it is free. The agent gets the task in its chat and reports the result with a tool; done without a result does not count, and you accept it. If the agent lacks something, it files a request for the task — the task waits for the answer and continues when it comes. A team member's task is accepted by the team lead (if one is set) or by you.
